sections.title: The problem
sections.body:
When a sending domain is disabled, **the reason is lost the moment it happens.** A detector flips `SendingDomain.disabled`, logs a free-text `disableCriterion` nobody reads, and leaves a `DisableDomainEvent` that says only "a domain was disabled".

- **Reviewers** reconstruct the why from thousands of inlined account-limit-notice cards.
- **Customers** see one generic "contact support"; the API says "No sending domain configured".
- **Re-enable is blunt:** Reenable overrides every flagged email the team ever sent; approving one flagged email re-enables a domain disabled for something unrelated — even a deliberate admin block.
- **Unleash** silently grants a permanent safety-check exemption.
- **Every ruling overwrites** `decision` in place, so a wrong call leaves no trace.

sections.title: The guiding question
sections.body:
> At any moment we can answer: why can't this team send, who decided that, and what would change it?

Rules that follow (signed off separately in the principles deck):
- **1** · A restriction is a claim with a reason and a decider — a person, or a named automation.
- **2** · The remedy matches the finding — restrict and allow at the same grain.
- **3** · A detector's verdict is provisional; a person's is binding.
- **4** · Record what happened once; compute everything else.

sections.title: Three nouns
sections.body:
```
Restriction
  teamId, sendingDomainId?          // null = the whole team
  category, ruleId?, findingKey?
  deciderKind (person | automation), deciderName
  liftedAt?, liftedByUserId?, liftVerdict? (wrong | fixed), liftNote?   // written once

Allowance                            // exactly one selector
  teamId
  category + findingKey  |  ruleId  |  category  |  (none = all checks)
  until, grantedByUserId, note
  revokedAt?, revokedByUserId?      // written once
```

- **Disabled** = the domain or its team has a restriction with no `liftedAt`. `SendingDomain.disabled` is the cache.
- **A lift** is `UPDATE … WHERE liftedAt IS NULL` — a second lift, or one from a stale page, does nothing.
- **The registry** (TS) holds categories and rules: subject, label, which finding type a rule produces.

sections.title: What the MVP is
sections.body:
**Every disable records a restriction that says why and who decided; every enable goes through a lift; the review page shows what's keeping a domain disabled; approving an email lifts only that email's restrictions.**

# Folded in from Codex's first review
- **Every enable is a lift** — admin Reenable and Unleash lift what's in effect, so the cache and the restrictions can't disagree.
- **Team scope** — SES pauses, suspicious signups and deletion restrict the team; a domain added later starts disabled.
- **Findings cite the email** — two flagged emails are two restrictions; approving one can't lift the other.

# Deliberately unchanged
- `DisableDomainEvent` is still written on a flip, as history; the review page reads restrictions.
- Allowances, the lift verdict dialog, snooze and `enforce` wait for later phases.

# What we learn
The real mix of categories; how often restrictions overlap; how often each gets lifted.

sections.title: 1 · The restriction table
sections.body:
**Band:** schema + queries.

- Migration: `Restriction` with CHECKs — `deciderKind = 'person' ⇒ ruleId IS NULL`; `deciderKind = 'automation' ⇒ ruleId IS NOT NULL`; `liftedAt IS NOT NULL ⇒ liftedByUserId, liftVerdict, liftNote IS NOT NULL`. Indexes on `(sendingDomainId, liftedAt)` and `(teamId, liftedAt)`. Squawk-clean.
- Queries (`queries/restriction.ts`): `create`, `listInEffectForDomain` (domain + its team), `listForDomain`, `lift(id, …)` as a guarded update.
- Tests (real DB): round-trip; a second lift changes nothing; a team-scoped restriction shows up for each of the team's domains; the CHECKs reject a person claim with a rule.

sections.title: 2 · The registry
sections.body:
**Band:** pure lib, unit tests.

```
// lib/enforcement/registry.ts
categories: content.phishing, content.unclassified, content.banned_word,
            behavior.complaint_rate, behavior.bounce_rate, behavior.provider_paused,
            account.suspicious_signup, account.new_domains_paused, account.deleted
rules:      phishing_classifier, classifier_unrecognized_output, banned_word_substring,
            health_complaint_limit, health_bounce_limit, ses_tenant_disabled,
            spammy_signup_pattern, new_domains_paused_flag, team_deletion
findings:   email:<id>, word:<lowercased>
```

Each rule names its one category and its finding type. Only what phase 1 reads is in it — labels, subject, finding type. Customer copy and policy arrive with the phases that read them.

sections.title: 3 · Every disable records a restriction
sections.body:
**Band:** model + its callers (the parameter is required, so callers land with it).

`SendingDomainModel.restrict({ teamId, sendingDomainId?, category, ruleId?, findingKey?, decider })`, in one transaction:
1. Lock the domain row (or the team row for a team claim).
2. An automation's claim with the same rule + finding already in effect → skip. A person's claim is always recorded.
3. Create the restriction; flip `disabled` on the affected domains; write `DisableDomainEvent` only on a flip, as today.

| Site | Decider | Category / rule | Finding | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| health cron | health-cron | complaint / bounce limit | — | domain |
| AI check ×4 | phishtank or ai-check | phishing_classifier / unrecognized | email | domain |
| banned words | banned-words | banned_word_substring | each word | domain |
| SES DISABLED | ses | ses_tenant_disabled | — | team |
| creation | domain-creation | signup pattern / pause flag | — | team |
| team deletion | team-deletion | team_deletion | — | team |
| admin mark unsafe | the admin | content.phishing | email | domain |
| bulk signup block | the admin | account.suspicious_signup | — | team |

Domain creation also checks the team: a new domain under a restricted team starts disabled.

sections.title: 4 · Every enable is a lift; admins say why they block
sections.body:
**Band:** model + the assessment flow.

- Reenable and Unleash lift every restriction in effect on the domain and its team (`liftVerdict: fixed` until the dialog lets the admin choose), then flip the cache. Unleash still sets `skipSafetyChecks` as today.
- Block requires the admin to pick a **category** (a small select in the assessment form, note required) and records a person's claim.
- Approving from the old queue keeps resolving the legacy event — history only.

This is where "re-enabling lifts an admin's block too" lands — derived state requires it, and the block survives as its own row with its lift.

sections.title: 5 · Show what's keeping it disabled
sections.body:
**Band:** wiring + UI.

- `getDomainInfo` returns the restrictions in effect: category label, rule, finding, decider, time.
- DomainReview opens with **Keeping this domain disabled**; the queue row shows the category.
- A domain disabled before phase 1 has none: the section says **Disabled before reasons were recorded**.

sections.title: 6 · Approving an email lifts only that email
sections.body:
**Band:** model + its one adoption site.

`approveEmail({ teamId, sendingDomainId, emailMessageId, adminUserId })`:
1. Lock; lift every restriction in effect whose finding is `email:<id>` (`liftVerdict: wrong`, note "approved flagged email").
2. Nothing left in effect → enable. Something left → return what still blocks.
3. Disabled before phase 1 (nothing recorded) → don't enable; return `unrecorded_disable` so the admin reviews it.

`overrideEmailMessage` still sets `override` on the email (today's mechanism), calls this, and names what still blocks.

sections.title: Phase 2 · Lift verdicts and allowances
sections.body:
- The lift dialog: **was it wrong, or did they fix it?** — plus an optional allowance at the narrowest grain: this finding → this rule for this team → this category for this team, with an end date.
- Automations check allowances before restricting; a suppressed finding is noted, not acted on.
- Allow a specific banned word for a team.
- Closes the "fires again right after a person lifted it" gap.

sections.title: Phase 3 · Notes and snooze
sections.body:
- A notes table on restrictions.
- Snooze (`awaiting_customer`, `cooling_off`, `probation`) with an end — as a field or a note kind, whichever the queue needs.
- Queue: paying first, age against the SLA; the account-limit-notice chart replaces the inlined cards.

sections.title: Phase 4 · One entry point for detectors
sections.body:
- `enforce` = the policy's `decide`, then write restrictions. safety-v0's `act` and a future safety-log policy call it.
- **The seam:** a policy changes sending state only by writing a restriction, and reads allowances as an input. Nothing in enforcement reads a policy, so policies can be added, versioned or deleted without touching restrictions.
- Detectors link their evidence; the decider name carries the version.
- `handleDisableNewDomain` is deleted.

sections.title: Phase 5 · Customer surfaces
sections.body: - Banner, notification email and API error (`sending_domain_disabled` + category) worded by subject through the registry.

sections.title: Later, when a case needs it
sections.body:
- Content holds keyed on a content hash; team publishing blocks.
- Idempotency keys.
- Policy replay against history.
- Retiring `safetyClassification = "override"` for content-scoped clearance.
